question: Can TealScript go all-in on codegen while keeping the React Native mobile port self-contained and at full feature parity?

closurePrototype.description: AST top-level statements are pre-bound to closures; expression and builtin semantics delegate to the existing engine so the prototype can run real external-corpus scripts without new Function.
limitations: This prototype did not bind expression nodes. The per-bar hot path still used the interpreter's expression dispatcher, operator handling, and series lookup.
Its interpreter-speed result is retained as historical data but must not be used to conclude that a real closure backend is interpreter-speed.

sample.selection: validity=supported, outputParity=matched, executionMode=compiled, no imports, no request/security calls

closurePrototype.conclusion: Superseded by T91. This shallow closure-tree prototype measured an interpreter hot path with closured top-level statements, so it did not test the no-eval backend hypothesis.

findings: React Native documentation says Hermes is used by default and that release builds compile JavaScript to Hermes bytecode.

The bundled hermesc binary is compiler-only in this install and reports that -exec is unsupported, so this repo cannot execute a Hermes runtime smoke without a native host or separately built Hermes shell.
hermesc accepts new Function under the default compiler settings and emits bytecode that constructs the global Function object.
hermesc accepts eval but warns that direct local eval lexical scope is unsupported.

Hermes Runtime.h documents a runtime enableEval flag that controls eval and the Function constructor. React Native's local Hermes runtime builders in node_modules do not set that flag explicitly, so the default must be verified in the consuming native app before claiming current compiled support on mobile.

quickJsProbe.limits: Measured in Node through the existing WASM QuickJS package, not through a React Native native JSI binding. It proves source compile and simple boundary costs are plausible, but not full TealScript execution or device binary cost.

requiresGeneratedJavaScriptSource: Native arithmetic, comparison, logical short-circuit, ternary, and literal/object/array expression lowering emit JavaScript expressions directly.
Control flow emits JavaScript if/else, for, while, break, continue, and generated loop-limit checks rather than data structures interpreted by a VM.
User-defined functions and imported functions are emitted as JavaScript methods with direct positional arguments, per-callsite source descriptors, and generated local/history state slots.
Persistent variables, series history, UDT fields, request state, drawing state, and strategy state are laid out as generated class fields and helper calls.
TA state uses generated class members and direct compute/recompute calls keyed by first-tick and bar-index state.
Runtime side effects for plot, alert, log, runtime.error, time/session, request, arrays, maps, matrices, drawings, and strategy route through generated helper calls.
stringEmitterDependencies.conclusion: The current compiler's speed comes from JavaScript source lowering across expression, control flow, call, state, and side-effect paths. Removing new Function without losing speed requires a real second backend or VM, not only replacing the final factory call.

recommendation.primary: Do not delete the interpreter until mobile compiled execution is proven in the native host. The cheapest next proof is a React Native Hermes smoke that directly runs TealScript's current generated Function path on-device/simulator, then benchmarks a representative corpus sample.

ifHermesFunctionWorks.option: Wire current source-codegen compiled execution into MobileIndicatorManager, without Worker, using the existing interpreter request/library seams and visible realtime fallback reasons.
ifHermesFunctionWorks.risk: Dynamic Function code is not precompiled into the app bundle and may run through a slower Hermes dynamic-eval/interpreter path; performance could be materially below web even if it executes.

ifHermesFunctionFailsOrIsTooSlow.option: Build a true non-eval backend, or embed a separate JS engine such as QuickJS for generated-source execution.
ifHermesFunctionFailsOrIsTooSlow.risk: A fast closure backend effectively duplicates most of the current source emitter; QuickJS adds native dependency/release-size/JSI ownership risk and still needs a device benchmark.

recommendation.largestUncertainty: The consuming mobile app's actual Hermes runtime behavior and performance for Function-constructor generated code; this repo has Tealchart source and RN packages but no app Podfile/Gradle runtime smoke.
